guard_streams.source: Signal struggles on trains widespread, Ofcom research finds
guard_streams.write_limit: Rail mobile-performance research concerns tested train segments and mobile networks. It cannot verify fixed-broadband coverage or speed at a selected parcel.

facts.detail: Ofcom published the rail mobile-performance findings on 3 June 2026.
The study measured 24 segments of key railway lines across England, Scotland and Wales.
Good performance required at least 5 Mbit/s down, 1.5 Mbit/s up and latency no more than 50 ms.
Poor performance occurred on between 58% and 83% of tests depending on network.
EE met the defined standard on 42% of measured rail segments.
Three met the standard on 21% of measured segments.
O2 met the standard on 20% of measured segments.
Vodafone met the standard on 17% of measured segments.
On-board Wi-Fi performed well only 1% of the time in the tests.
The report identifies weak trackside signal and signal-blocking carriage types as core problems.

guard_streams.source: Switching off 2G and 3G networks: advice for IoT and third-party device suppliers
guard_streams.write_limit: 2G/3G migration timetables and predicted mobile not-spots are mobile-device continuity evidence. They do not establish fixed-broadband parcel coverage.

facts.detail: Ofcom published the supplier advice on 22 January 2024.
The page was last updated on 19 June 2026.
The page states that UK 3G mobile networks are now switched off.
It states that 2G networks will be switched off over the next few years.
EE announced that it will begin switching off 2G from May 2029.
VodafoneThree announced a Vodafone 2G switch-off during 2030.
O2 announced that its 2G switch-off will start in summer 2029.
O2 began withdrawing 2G access for inbound roaming services from 1 October 2025.
The Government published a voluntary 2G switch-off charter in March 2026.
Providers using affected equipment are advised to upgrade to at least 4G-capable devices.

guard_streams.source: Electromagnetic field measurements near mobile base stations
guard_streams.write_limit: EMF audits measure exposure near mobile masts. They do not demonstrate broadband coverage, orderability or parcel-specific network performance.

facts.detail: Ofcom published the EMF audit page on 23 February 2024.
The page was last updated on 26 June 2026.
Ofcom says it has measured EMF near mobile base stations for many years.
Repeat measurements are taken in Belfast, Cardiff, Liverpool and London.
Repeat audits under steady conditions support observation of changes over time.
Published measurements have shown levels well within general-public EMF limits.
The page provides a test report for each visited location.
It includes monopole-mast measurements for Cambridge, Hatfield and Luton.
The page lists multiple January 2026 survey locations.
Ofcom reports 38 surveys near 5G-enabled base stations between April and October 2021.

guard_streams.source: Requesting surveys of EMF emissions from mobile base stations
guard_streams.write_limit: Requested EMF surveys verify exposure against ICNIRP limits, not fixed-broadband availability or measured internet service.

facts.detail: Ofcom published the EMF survey-request page on 2 January 2024.
The surveys verify emissions against ICNIRP general-public exposure levels.
The service is available to members of the public concerned about exposure near their home.
Ofcom also carries out surveys for schools and hospitals.
The surveys are not conducted for use as evidence in commercial transactions.
They are not intended for Wireless Telegraphy Act licensees to self-check equipment compliance.
The stated charge is £1,000 excluding VAT.
Schools and hospitals may receive a survey free subject to resources and conditions.
A request includes the applicant's name, location including postcode and contact details.
Results go to the requester; Ofcom may publish selected information while protecting requester identity and exact address.
